question.text: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations governing NAV computation at Cat I/II AIFs, the NAV calculation function must be:

answer.text: Performed by the fund manager's internal team to ensure accuracy
Independent from the fund management function
Performed only by the fund's statutory auditor
Shared equally between the Manager and Trustee

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.10: 'As per SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, every AIF shall ensure that calculation of the Net Asset Value (NAV) is INDEPENDENT from its fund management function.' This typically means outsourced to a fund administrator or performed by a segregated team. The Trap: Internal team inside fund management creates conflicts; statutory auditor is a post-hoc check not an ongoing NAV computation; Manager-Trustee shared responsibility is not the regulatory structure. The principle is INDEPENDENCE from fund management. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical segregation. XXI-B has similar custodian/accounting segregation for PMS. Mutual Fund Regulations (tested in V-A) have the strictest NAV-independence rules. Manager's Pro-Tip: Outsource NAV computation to a specialist fund administrator (e.g., IQ-EQ, Apex, Kfintech) from day one. Your annual LP report should name the administrator and their SOC-1 audit status — institutional LPs ask this in ODD (operational due diligence).
